analog_input_absolute_maximum.document: ST STM32H742xI/G STM32H743xI/G datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3
analog_input_absolute_maximum.shows: Table 20, Voltage characteristics: input voltage on TT_xx pins is -0.3 to 4.0 V absolute maximum. Not VDD + 0.3: the TT_xx row states a flat 4.0 V of its own, where the FT_xxx row above it is written as a formula on the supplies. This is the ceiling the analog sense inputs are held to, and the reason the analog rail out of the connector is regulated to 3.3 V rather than clamped.

analog_input_injection_current.document: ST STM32H742xI/G STM32H743xI/G datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3
analog_input_injection_current.shows: Table 21, Current characteristics: injected current on FT_xxx, TT_xx, RST and B pins except PA4, PA5 is -5/+0 mA, and note 3 reads verbatim 'Positive injection is not possible on these I/Os and does not occur for input voltages lower than the specified maximum value.' So there is no positive-injection allowance to be inside of, and the 4.0 V of Table 20 is a limit with nothing below it.

current_consumption_scheme.document: ST STM32H742xI/G STM32H743xI/G datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3
current_consumption_scheme.shows: Figure 14, Current consumption measurement scheme: the I_DD ammeter feeds a node that branches to BOTH V_DD and V_DDA. So the I_DD figures in Table 29 - including the 500 mA this board budgets for the MCU at 400 MHz VOS1 with all peripherals enabled - already include the analog supply. VDDA is not a separate load to add to the 3V3 rail's sum. Only V_BAT is metered separately, and this board ties it to the rail.

power_dissipation_at_85c.document: STMicroelectronics STM32H743xI datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3 (October 2017), served by LCSC for C114408
power_dissipation_at_85c.shows: Table 23: power dissipation at T_A = 85 degC for the suffix 6 version, 915 mW in the LQFP144 row, and the suffix 6 ambient range of -40 to 85 degC at maximum power dissipation. 85 + 0.915 x 43.7 = 125, so ST's own three figures are consistent with the 125 degC junction limit and this is what pins that down.

power_supply_scheme.document: STMicroelectronics STM32H743xI datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3 (October 2017), served by LCSC for C114408
power_supply_scheme.shows: Figure 13, Power supply scheme, with each decoupling value against the pin it belongs to: VDD gets N x 100 nF plus one 4.7 uF where N is the package's VDD pin count, VCAP 2 x 2.2 uF, VDDLDO 4.7 uF, VDDA 100 nF + 1 uF, VREF+ 100 nF + 1 uF, and VDD33USB and VDD50USB 100 nF each

rmii_conditions.assumes: Nothing on the board sets OSPEEDR. It is a firmware constraint, recorded in the pin map.
rmii_conditions.document: ST STM32H742xI/G STM32H743xI/G datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3
rmii_conditions.shows: The conditions Table 111 is measured under: output speed set to OSPEEDRy[1:0] = 10, capacitive load C = 20 pF, measurement points at 0.5 VDD. The 11.5 ns td(TXD) maximum is a high-drive figure - at the reset default it is not specified at all, which is the documented cause of RMII CRC errors on this MCU.

rmii_timing.document: ST STM32H742xI/G STM32H743xI/G datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3
rmii_timing.shows: Table 111, Dynamics characteristics: Ethernet MAC signals for RMII. td(TXD) transmit data valid delay 7 / 7.5 / 11.5 ns, td(TXEN) 4 / 4.5 / 7, tsu(RXD) 2 ns minimum, tih(RXD) 3 ns minimum, tsu(CRS) 2.5, tih(CRS) 2. Guaranteed by characterization results. These are the MCU's half of the RMII budget, which this board's RMII check said ST does not state.

thermal_characteristics.document: STMicroelectronics STM32H743xI datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3 (October 2017), served by LCSC for C114408
thermal_characteristics.shows: Section 7.9's equation T_J max = T_A max + (P_D max x theta_JA) and Table 126 beside it, where the LQFP144 20x20 mm 0.5 mm pitch row reads 43.7 degC/W. It is the figure the board's declared ambient is derived from.

vref_against_vdda.document: ST STM32H742xI/G STM32H743xI/G datasheet, DocID030538 Rev 3
vref_against_vdda.shows: Table 86: VREF+ positive reference voltage, minimum 1.80 V and **maximum VDDA**. The relationship is a recommended operating condition and not an absolute maximum - Table 20 has no VREF-to-VDDA row at all and treats VREF+ as one of the 4.0 V 'any other pins'. It is the constraint the power-up deck holds the rails to at every instant of the ramp rather than only in steady state, which is what commit c297e58 violated for a millisecond with nothing on the board able to see it.
